83. Shri Kumbhandas Ji Varta (Ashtasakha 3)

Now we relate the essence (Bhava) of the Varta of Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji's sevak, Kumbhandasji—a Gorva Kshatriya residing in Jamunavata—whose sacred kirtan pads are sung among the Ashtachhap.

Bhavprakash — In eternal Lila, Kumbhandasji is the manifestation of Shri Thakorji's intimate sakha 'Arjun.' In daytime Lila he is Arjun Sakha, and in nighttime Nikunj Lila he is 'Vishakhaji,' the intimate sakhi of Shri Swaminiji. Vishakhaji's other manifestation is Krishnadas Meghan, who always accompanied Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji on his Prithvi Parikrama, while Kumbhandasji always remained with Shri Govardhannathji. Thus, in sakha-bhava Kumbhandasji is Arjun, and in sakhi-bhava he is Vishakha.

Shri Girirajji has eight gates, one of which is near Anyor at Jamunavata; Kumbhandasji is the Mukhiya (chief attendant) of Seva at that gate. The village is called 'Jamunavata' because in the Saraswat Kalpa, Shri Yamunaji flowed in two streams—one via Jamunavata toward Agra and the other via Cheerghat toward Shri Gokul, merging further ahead. A branch flowed from Cheerghat to Shri Girirajji; hence the Raslila of the Rasapanchadhyayi took place at Chandrasarovar in Parasoli. During the disappearance (Antardhan) Lila, the Brajbhaktas inquired of the trees and vines from Chandrasarovar via Govindkund to Apsarakund, where they saw Shri Thakorji's footprints. Going further, Shri Thakorji braided Radha Sahachari's hair and adorned her with sindoor and kajal—hence the Sinduri, Kajali, and Bajani Shilas there. Further at Rudrakund, Radha Sahachari felt pride (maan) and said she could walk no further; under the pretext of lifting her onto His shoulders, Shri Thakorji vanished beneath a tree. Radha Sahachari wept:
"Haa Natha Ramanapreshtha Kvasi Kvasi Mahabhuja |
Dasyaste Kripaya Me Sakhe Darshaya Sannidhim ||"
("O Lord, dearest Beloved, O mighty-armed one, where are You? Out of compassion, O friend, reveal Your presence to Your maidservant!")
Hence that pond is called 'Rudrakund.' All the Gopis then gathered, inquired of the 'Jaan' and 'Ajaan' trees, and reached the banks of Shri Yamunaji at Jamunavata, where they sang the Gopika Geet ('Jayati Te'dhikam...') in tears. Shri Thakorji then reappeared, performed the Raslila at Parasoli Chandrasarovar, and enjoyed Jal-vihar in Shri Yamunaji. Earlier, seeing dense darkness ahead while searching, they had turned back ('Tamah Pravishtamalakshya Tato Nivavriturhareh')—that dark grove is Shyamvan near Samai village beyond Shyamdhak. Thus, while the Shwetavaraha Kalpa Ras took place at Vansivat in Vrindavan, the principal autumn Ras of the Saraswat Kalpa occurred at Parasoli near Shri Girirajji, leaving the sacred signs of Shri Yamunaji's presence near Jamunavata and Sanket to strengthen the faith of devotees.

Varta — Prasang 1
Kumbhandasji lived in Jamunavata and farmed his ancestral fields at Parasoli Chandrasarovar. Unattached to worldly household life from childhood, he never spoke a lie or committed any sinful act, living as a simple, guileless Brajvasi. When he grew up, he married at Bahulavan near Jait village. Though his wife was an ordinary soul rather than a lila-sambandhi, the association (Satsang) of a supreme Bhagavadiya like Kumbhandasji never goes in vain, so she too attained upliftment.

At that time, Shri Govardhannathji had not yet been manifested upon Shri Girirajji. Once, while Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji was in Jharkhand in the south during his Prithvi Parikrama, Shri Govardhannathji commanded him: "I have manifested at Shri Govardhan; come bring Me forth and reveal My Seva to the world." Leaving his parikrama right there, Shri Acharyaji went straight to Braj with five sevaks: Damodardas Harsani, Krishnadas Meghan, Madhav Bhatt, Narayandas, and Ramdas of Sikandarpur. Shri Acharyaji seated himself on the platform (chautara) at Sadu Pande's door in Anyor, initiated Sadu Pande, Manikchand Pande, Naro, and Bhavani, and entrusted Shri Govardhannathji's Seva to Ramdas Chauhan (who lived in a cave near Puchhari).

Hearing in Jamunavata that a great Mahapurush had arrived in Anyor, manifested Shri Govardhannathji, and accepted many Brajvasis as sevaks, Kumbhandasji told his wife: "Let us go to Anyor and become Shri Acharyaji's sevaks; by his grace, Shri Thakorji will shower grace upon us." His wife agreed, thinking: "I have no son; if this great soul grants one, I shall have a son." Both went to Anyor and offered Dandavat to Shri Acharyaji. Seeing him, Shri Acharyaji immediately said, "Kumbhandas! You have come?" Being a daivi jiva, Kumbhandasji instantly recognized Shri Acharyaji's divine swaroop and pleaded, "Maharaj! I have wandered for so long; now please bestow Your grace upon me."

Shri Acharyaji had both bathe in Sankarshankund and granted them Naam and Brahmasambandh. Then Kumbhandasji's wife prayed, "Maharaj! You are great; I have no son, please grant me one." Pleased, Shri Acharyaji blessed her: "Do not worry, you shall have seven sons." Overjoyed, she stepped back, but Kumbhandasji chided her: "What did you ask of Shri Acharyaji? Had you asked for Shri Thakorji, he would have given you Shri Thakorji Himself!" She replied, "I asked for what I wanted; you may ask for what you want." Kumbhandasji remained silent.

Shri Acharyaji then built a small temple atop Giriraj, installed Shri Govardhannathji, and instructed Sadu Pande, Kumbhandasji, and all Brajvasi sevaks: "Shri Govardhannathji is our everything; stay devoted to His Seva and never take Mahaprasad without having His darshan." Knowing Kumbhandasji's melodious voice and gift for kirtan, Shri Acharyaji entrusted him with singing daily kirtans for Shri Govardhannathji at each time of Seva. Waking Shri Govardhannathji the next morning, Shri Acharyaji asked Kumbhandasji to sing of Bhagavad-lila. Offering Dandavat to Shri Govardhannathji, Kumbhandasji sang his very first pad:

Raag Bilawal —
"Saanjh ke saanche bol tihare |
Rajani anat jage Nandanandan aaye nipat savare ||1||
Aatur bhae neelpat odhe peeyare basan bisare |
'Kumbhandas Prabhu' Govardhandhar bhale bachan pratipare ||2||"
(True are Your words of last evening! Having stayed awake elsewhere all night, Nandanandan has arrived at the break of dawn, hastily draped in a blue garment while forgetting His yellow one! Kumbhandas's Lord Govardhandhar keeps His promises so well!)

Hearing this kirtan, Shri Acharyaji asked, "Kumbhandas! Have you experienced the rasa of Nikunj-lila?" Bowing, Kumbhandasji replied, "Maharaj, by Your grace." Shri Acharyaji said, "Great is your fortune that the Lord has first revealed to you the power of His grace (Prameya-bal); you shall forever remain immersed in Hari-rasa." Kumbhandasji prayed that he might always be blessed with this supreme rasa alone. Accordingly, all of Kumbhandasji's kirtans celebrate the Yugal Swaroop and Nikunj-lila; he never sang Badhai, Palna, or Bal-lila pads. Thereafter, Shri Acharyaji resumed his Prithvi Parikrama.

Varta — Prasang 2
Kumbhandasji walked daily from Jamunavata to Shri Girirajji for Shri Govardhannathji's darshan and kirtan. Shri Govardhannathji showed him direct intimacy, playing and conversing with him. After some time, a hostile Mleccha invader approached from the west, plundering villages, and camped five kos from Shri Girirajji. The four intimate Vaishnavas—Sadu Pande, Manikchand Pande, Ramdasji, and Kumbhandasji—went into the temple and asked Shri Govardhannathji what to do. Shri Nathji commanded: "Take Me to 'Tond ke Ghane' (the dense thicket of Tond); I wish to go there." When they asked what mount to arrange, Shri Nathji said: "Bring the male buffalo (bhainsa) from Sadu Pande's house; I shall ride upon it."

Bhavprakash — That buffalo was a daivi jiva. In eternal Lila, she was Vrinda, the gardener (malin) of Shri Vrishabhanuji's garden who brought fresh flower garlands daily. Once when Shri Swaminiji visited the garden, Vrinda remained seated feeding her daughter and failed to rise or offer Dandavat. When Shri Swaminiji asked her to carry a message to Shri Nandarayji's house, she refused on the pretext of making garlands. Shri Swaminiji cursed her to be born as a buffalo on earth. Falling at her feet in supplication, Vrinda was blessed that when Shri Thakorji rode upon her into the forest, she would be accepted and restored to her sakhi form as gardener. Thus she was born as Sadu Pande's buffalo.

Shri Govardhannathji rode the buffalo into Tond ke Ghane. Ramdasji and Sadu Pande supported Him on either side, while Kumbhandasji and Manikchand Pande cleared thorny vines ahead. Thorns pricked them severely and tore their clothes. Inside Tond ke Ghane lay a lovely nikunj with a small lake and a circular platform (chautara). Spreading the cushion (gadi) from the buffalo onto the platform, they seated Shri Nathji. Ramdasji had hastily prepared two sers of wheat-flour sira; at Shri Nathji's command, he offered the entire amount as Bhog, and all four Vaishnavas stepped behind a tree.

Then Shri Swaminiji arrived in the nikunj bringing delicacies she had personally cooked, and both dined together. Noticing Shri Swaminiji was slightly tired from cooking, Shri Govardhannathji called to Kumbhandasji: "Kumbhandas! Sing a kirtan now to delight our hearts." Sensing the Lord desired light humor—and since all four Vaishnavas were hungry and scratched by thorns—Kumbhandasji sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Bhavat hai tohi Tond kau ghano |
Kaanta lage gokharu bhage phatyo jaat yah tano ||1||
Sinhe kaha lonkari kau dar yah kaha baanik banyo |
'Kumbhandas' tum Govardhandhar vah kaun raand dhedhani kau janyo ||2||"
(How fond You are of the dense thicket of Tond! Thorns and burrs prick us and tear our bodies! What fear does a lion have of a fox—what kind of disguise is this? O Govardhandhar, says Kumbhandas, who is that lowly creature You are pretending to flee?)

Shri Govardhannathji, Shri Swaminiji, and all the Vaishnavas laughed with delight. At Mala time, Kumbhandasji sang:

Raag Malkauns —
"Bolat Syam manohar baithe kamal khand aur kadam ki chhaiyan |
Kusumit drum ali peek goonjat kokila kal gaavat tahiyan ||1||
Sunat dutika ke bachan madhuri bhayo hulaas tan man mahiyan |
Kumbhandas Prabhu Braj juvati milan thali rasik kunvar Giridhar pahiyan ||2||"
(Seated in the shade of lotuses and kadamba trees, enchanting Shyam speaks sweetly while bees hum and cuckoos sing among blossoming trees. Hearing the messenger's sweet words fills body and heart with rapture at this trysting-place of Braj's maidens with the Rasik prince Giridhar!)

Shri Swaminiji then asked Shri Govardhannathji how He had come. Hearing of Sadu Pande's buffalo, she cast her merciful gaze upon it and declared: "She is my garden's malin, born as a buffalo for disobeying me; today she has performed noble Seva, so her offense is forgiven." After enjoying various lilas in Tond ke Ghane, Shri Swaminiji returned to Barsana.

Bhavprakash — To the doubt of how Shri Swaminiji walked amid thorns: the trees of Braj are swaroopatmak (divine in essence)—they appear thorny only to worldly eyes, while becoming fragrant bowers of flowers and fruits for the Divine Couple. And the four intimate Vaishnavas stepped behind a tree so Shri Swaminiji could serve Shri Nathji playfully without shyness.

Shri Nathji then called the four Vaishnavas back. Going out, Sadu Pande learned that the invader's army had retreated. Seating Shri Govardhannathji once more on the buffalo, they escorted Him back to His temple atop Shri Girirajji. Upon descending the hill, the buffalo shed its body and re-entered eternal Lila. Overjoyed at Shri Nathji's return, the Brajvasis praised Devdaman for averting the calamity in an instant. Kumbhandasji sang two celebratory pads in Raag Shrirag:

Raag Shrirag —
"Jayati jayati Haridasvaryadharane |
Vaari vrishti nivari, ghokh aarati taari Devapati maan bhang karane ||1||
Jayati pat peet damini ruchir var mridul ang saaval jalad varane |
Kar adhar benu dhari gaan kal-rav sabda sahaj Braj yuvati jan chitta harane ||2||
Jayati Vrinda vipin bhumi dolani akhil lok-vandani amburuh charane |
Tarani-tanaya-teer vihar Nandagop-kumar 'Daskumbhan' namit tuva sharane ||3||"

Raag Shrirag —
"Krishna tarani tanaya teer Rasmandal rachyo adhar kar madhur sur benu baaje |
Juvati jan jooth sang nartat anek rang nirakhi abhiman taji Kaam laaje ||1||
Syamatan peet kausheya subh pad-nakh-chandrika sakal bhuv timir bhaaje |
Lalit avatans bhuv bhu dhanus lochan chapal chitavani manon madanbaan saaje ||2||
Mukhar manjeer kati kinkini kuneet rav vachan gambhir manu megh gaaje |
'Das Kumbhan' nath Haridasvaryadharan nakhasikh swaroop adbhut biraaje ||3||"

Varta — Prasang 3
Kumbhandasji's pads became famous far and wide. A court musician (kalavat) learned one of his pads and sang it before Emperor Akbar at Fatehpur Sikri:

Raag Dhanashri —
"Dekhari aavani Madan Gopal ki |
Sakravahan-gati nirakh laajat gajagati anoop latak chaal ki ||1||
Syam tan kati basan man haran sundarata ur shrimaal ki |
Bhonh dhanus saji manahu Madan sar chitavani lochan visaal ki ||2||
Renumandit kuntal-alak sobha kesar kau tilak bhaal ki |
'Das Kumbhan' charu ras mohe jagat Govardhandhar kunvar rasaal ki ||3||"

Deeply captivated, Emperor Akbar asked where this great saint lived. Learning that Kumbhandasji lived in Jamunavata near Shri Govardhan, Akbar dispatched attendants with horses and a palanquin to bring him. They found Kumbhandasji seated in his field at Parasoli Chandrasarovar and delivered the Emperor's summons. Kumbhandasji replied: "We are poor Brajvasis, servants of no one; what business do we have with the Emperor?" The messengers begged him, saying Akbar would have them executed if they returned without him. Accepting it as an unavoidable trial, Kumbhandasji refused the horse and palanquin and walked all the way to Fatehpur Sikri on foot in worn-out shoes.

Dressed in a simple taniya, tattered soiled turban, pichhora, and broken shoes, Kumbhandasji stood inside Akbar's bejeweled, perfumed pavilion. Though Akbar welcomed him respectfully, Kumbhandasji felt as if sitting in living hell, longing for the trees of Braj where Shri Govardhandhar plays. When Akbar requested a Vishnupad, Kumbhandasji thought: "This Mleccha has separated me from Shri Govardhannathji; I cannot sing the Lord's lila before him." Holding firm to the faith that "When Manmohan accepts someone, not a single hair on their head falls even if the whole world turns hostile," he immediately sang his immortal pad:

Raag Sarang —
"Bhaktan kon kaha Sikri kaam |
Aavat jaat panhaiya tooti bisar gayo Hari naam ||1||
Jako mukh dekhe dukh upaje taakon karano paryo pranaam |
'Kumbhandas' Lal Giridhar binu yah sab jhootho dhaam ||2||"
(What business do devotees have with Sikri? Walking to and fro wore out my shoes and made me forget Hari's Name! I had to bow to one whose very sight brings sorrow. Without Giridhar Lal, says Kumbhandas, all this grand court is a false abode!)

Akbar felt stung at first, but soon realized Kumbhandasji had no worldly greed and cared only for God. He humbly asked, "Baba Sahib! Please grant me some command I may fulfill." Kumbhandasji replied, "From this day on, never summon me again." Akbar respectfully bade him farewell.

Walking back in intense separation (viraha) from Shri Govardhannathji, Kumbhandasji sang:

Raag Dhanashri —
"Kab haun dekhi hon in nainanu |
Sundar Syam manohar moorati ang ang sukh dainanu ||1||
Vrindavan vihar din din prati gop-vrind sang lenanu |
Hansi hansi harakhi patauvani peevanu baanti baanti paya phenanu ||2||
'Kumbhandas' kete din bite kiye rain sukh sainanu |
Ab Giridhar binu nisi aru baasar man na parat kachu chainanu ||3||"

Two prahars felt like two yugas. Climbing Shri Girirajji and beholding Shri Govardhannathji's face wiped away all sorrow, and he sang:

Raag Dhanashri —
"Nain bhari dekhyo Nandakumar |
Ta din ten sab bhooli gai haun bisaryo pati-parivar ||1||
Binu dekhe haun bibas bhai ri ang-ang sab haari |
Taaten sudhi hai saavari moorati lochan bhari bhari vaari ||2||
Rooparasi parimit nahin maanon kaise mile Kanhai |
'Kumbhandas Prabhu' Govardhandhar mili bahuri ur laai ||3||"

Raag Dhanashri —
"Hilagan kathin hai ya man ki |
Jaake liye dekhi meri sajani laaj gai sab tan ki ||1||
Dharam jaau aur log hasau sab, aru aavo kul-gaari |
So kyon rahe taahi binu dekhe jo jaakau hitakaari ||2||
Ras-lubdha ek nimish nahin chhaandat jyon adheen mrig gaane |
'Kumbhandas' yah saneh maram kau Shri Govardhandhar jaane ||3||"

Shri Govardhannathji said, "Kumbhandas! You are blessed. Just as you find no peace for a moment without Me, I too find no joy without you." Such was their mutual love.

Varta — Prasang 4
Once Raja Man Singh, returning victorious from campaigns via Agra, stopped in Mathura and Vrindavan during the scorching month of Jyeshtha. Knowing of his arrival, the priests and mahants had draped their deities in heavy zari brocade and gold ornaments. Man Singh quietly thought this was merely ostentation to impress him.

Arriving at Shri Govardhan in the afternoon, Man Singh climbed the hill barefoot in the blistering heat just as the doors opened for Bhog darshan. Cooled by rosewater, fragrant with argaja, fanned by double fans, and adorned in a light white turban, pardani, and delicate pearl ornaments, Shri Govardhannathji's darshan soothed every pore of Man Singh's body. He exclaimed: "True Seva is here! The very Shri Krishna of Shrimad Bhagavatam resides here!" At that moment Kumbhandasji was singing:

Raag Nat —
"Roop dekhi nainaan palak lage nahin |
Govardhandhar ke ang ang prati nirakhi nain man rahat tahin ||1||
Kaha ri kahon kachu kahat na aave chitta choryo ve maang dahin |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu ke miliveki sundar baat sakhiyan son ju kahi ||2||"

Raag Nat —
"Pootari poriya inke bhae ri maai |
Ko roke ya mag aavat khanjan chhori dae palak na kapaat diye ri maai ||1||
Thaadhe rahat prem ke baadhe nisabaasar sab sukh chitae ri maai |
'Kumbhandas' Lal Giridharan man ke bhaajan phori dhandhori liye ri maai ||2||"

Raag Shrirag —
"Aavat Giridhar man joo harashyo ho |
Hon apane ghar sachu son baithi nirakhi vadan achara bisaryo ho ||1||
Roop nidhaan rasik Nandanandan nirakhi nain dheeraj na dharyo ho |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu Govardhandhar ang ang prem peeyush bharyo ho ||2||"

At Shayan Aarti, Kumbhandasji sang:
Raag Kedaro —
"Lal ke badan par aarati vaaron |
Chaaru chitavani karon saaj neeki yukti baati aganit ghrit kapoor so baaron ||1||
Sankh dhuni bheri-mridang jhaalar jhaanjh taal ghanta baaje bahut vistaaron |
Gaaoon saamal sujas rasana sukhasvaad ras param harakh tan chamar kar daaron ||2||
Koti udyot ravikaanti ang ang chhabi sakal bhoolok ko timir taaron |
'Daskumbhan' piya Lal Giridharan ko roop dekhi nayanan bhari bhari nihaaron ||3||"

Returning to his camp, Man Singh inquired about the singer and next morning came during Giriraj parikrama to Parasoli Chandrasarovar. At that very moment, Shri Govardhannathji was sitting in Kumbhandasji's lap about to tell him something! Seeing Man Singh approach, Shri Nathji ran and hid behind a tree. Kumbhandasji kept gazing at that tree, not even glancing at the Raja who bowed and sat nearby. Just then Kumbhandasji's niece arrived from Jamunavata carrying bejhari flour in a wooden bowl (kathoti) and said, "Baba, the Raja is sitting here; say something to him." Kumbhandasji grumbled, "What can I do? The One who was talking to me ran away because of him!" Silently gesturing, Shri Nathji reassured him that He would tell him later.

Kumbhandasji then asked his niece for his seat (asan) and mirror (arsi) to apply tilak. She replied, "Baba, the buffalo calf ate the grass asan and drank the water from the kathoti!" She brought a fresh bundle of grass and a bowl of water; sitting on the grass, Kumbhandasji looked at his reflection in the water and applied tilak. Astounded by such renunciation, Raja Man Singh offered a gold bejeweled mirror, a bag of 1,000 gold mohurs, a grant of Jamunavata village, and asked for his grocer's (modi's) name to supply him for life.

Kumbhandasji declined everything: "In a thatched hut, a gold mirror would invite someone to kill me; my farm provides what I eat; I am not a Brahmin to accept land grants." Pointing to a karil bush and a ber tree, he said: "In summer, karil is my grocer, giving flowers and tenti berries; in winter, the ber tree gives jujubes—thus I get by!" Bowing, Man Singh begged for just one command. Kumbhandasji said: "Never come to me again, and never speak to me again." Offering Dandavat, Man Singh declared: "I have traveled the whole earth and seen countless devotees of Maya, but you are the only true devotee of Shri Thakorji I have ever seen."

After Man Singh left, the niece playfully asked why he had refused the Raja's gifts when they had so little. Kumbhandasji gently admonished her: "Daughter, never speak of taking from anyone, even in jest, lest Shri Govardhannathji hear and be displeased!" Immediately, Shri Govardhannathji returned to Kumbhandasji's lap, and Kumbhandasji sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Param bhaanvate jiyake Mohan nainan ten mati taro |
Jo lon jeeoon to lon dekho baar baar pai laagon chitta anat na dharon ||1||
Tab sukh chintat tohi lon le le ang bharon |
Rasikan maanjh rasik-Nandanandan tum piya mere sakal dukh haro ||2||
Aavahu sada raho ghar mere Syam manohar sang kin karo |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu Govardhandhar tum binu anjan kaason karon ||3||"

Shri Govardhannathji then revealed what He had come to say: "Today the sakhas have a wager on whose home has the finest meal; I crave jwar ki maheri, curd, milk, bejhari roti, and tenti saag-sandhano." Kumbhandasji sent his niece for the pot of milk and ground jwar, and cooked bejhari roti on an earthen griddle along with jwar maheri. All the sakhas' lunch bundles (chhak) arrived, and Shri Nathji joyfully ate Kumbhandasji's simple meal and shared it with the sakhas (Bhavprakash notes Vishakhaji sweetened it with mishri for Shri Swaminiji). Filled with bliss, Kumbhandasji sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Braj men bado meva yah tenti |
Jaakau hot hai saag sandhano aur bejar ki rotau ||1||
Le le daliya beenan nikasi bade gop ki beti |
'Kumbhandas' Lal Giridhar son vhai gai bheta bheti ||2||"

Raag Sarang —
"Ghar ghar ten aai hai chhaak |
Khaate meethe aur salone vividh bhaanti ke paak ||1||
Mandal rachana kari Jamuna tat saghan lata ki chhaanh |
Gopi-gwaal sakal mili jemata mukh hi sarahat jaanh ||2||
Baantat Bal Mohan dou bhaiya kar dona ati sohe |
Chaakhat aapun sakhan mukhan de ke gopijan man mohe ||3||
Tenti, saag, sandhano roti, goras, saras maheri |
'Kumbhandas' Giridhar ras-lampat naachat dede pheri ||4||"

Absorbed in rasa all day, he realized at evening he had missed temple darshan, hurried up to the temple for Shayan darshan, and gazing intently sang:

Raag Bihag —
"Lochan mili gae jab chaaryo |
Hon vhai rahi thagi si thaadhi ur achara na sanvaaryo ||1||
Apane subhaai Nand joo ke aai sundar Syam nihaaryo |
Ik tak lagi charan gati thaaki kyon hoo tarat nahin taaryo ||2||
Upaji preeti Madan Mohan son griha kau kaaj bisaryo |
'Kumbhandas' Giridhar ras lobhi bhalo aaraj panth paaryo ||3||"

Raag Bihagaro —
"Nandanandan ki bali jaiye |
Saanval mridul kalevar ki chhabi dekhi dekhi sukh paiye ||1||
Sakal lokapati Thakur rasana rasik vimal jas gaiye |
'Kumbhandas Prabhu' Giridhar kon tan man sarvasva daiye ||2||"

Raag Kedaro —
"Chhinu chhinu baanik aur hi aur |
Jab dekhon tab nautan sakhiri drishti na rahe ikathaur ||1||
Kaha kahon paramit nahin paavat bohot karon chit daur |
'Kumbhandas Prabhu' saubhag seenva Giridhar rasikaraaya sir mor ||2||"

Varta — Prasang 5
Once the saints and mahants of Vrindavan, including Harivansh and Haridas, came to Shri Girirajji to meet Kumbhandasji. They said: "We have heard many of your pads on the Yugal Swaroop, but none exclusively on Shri Swaminiji; please sing one for us." Kumbhandasji then sang:

Raag Ramkali —
"Kunvari Radhike tuva sakal saubhagya seenva ya badan par koti sat chand vaari daaron |
Khanjan kurang sat koti nainan upar vaarane karat jiyamen bichaaron ||1||
Kadali sat koti janghan upar sinha sat koti kati par nyochhavar kari utaaron |
Matta gaj koti sat chaal par kumbh sat koti in kuchan par vaari daaron ||2||
Keer sat koti naasika upar kund sat koti dasanan upar kaahe na vaaron |
Pakva kindoor bandhook sat koti adharan upar vaari ruchi garva taaron ||3||
Naag sat koti beni upar kapot sat koti greeva doori saaron |
Kamal sat koti kar-jugal par vaarane naahin koou upama ju dhaaron ||4||
'Daskumbhan' Swamini sunakh-sikh adbhut sudhaan kahaan lon sambhaaron |
Lal Giridhar kahat mohi tohi lon sukh jo lonye roop chhinu chhinu nihaaron ||5||"

The Vrindavan saints were amazed and declared: "In our pads we compared Shri Swaminiji to the moon, but Kumbhandasji, you have sacrificed a billion moons to her beauty, finding nothing in the universe worthy of comparison!"

Varta — Prasang 6
Once Shri Gusainji planned a journey to Shri Dwarkaji for the upliftment of daivi jivas. Hearing from a Vaishnava that Kumbhandasji faced financial strain—supporting seven sons, seven daughters-in-law, his wife, his niece, and visiting Vaishnavas from meager farming—Shri Gusainji privately invited Kumbhandasji to join him so his household needs would be eased and he could enjoy Vaishnava satsang.

Out of obedience, Kumbhandasji joined after Rajbhog Aarti and camped with Shri Gusainji at Apsarakund. When Utthapan time arrived, intense separation (viraha) from Shri Govardhannathji overcame Kumbhandasji; tears streamed down his face, his hair stood on end, and standing under a tree he softly sang:

Raag Sarang —
"Kite din vhai ju gae binu dekhe |
Tarun kisor rasik Nandanandan kachhuk uthat mukh rekhe ||1||
Yah sobha vah kaanti badan ki kotik chand bisekhe |
Vah chitavani vah haasya manohar vah natavar vapu bhekhe ||2||
Syamasundar sang mili khelan ki aavat jiya apekhen |
Kumbhandas Lal Giridhar binu jeevan janma alekhe ||3||"

Overhearing from inside the tent, Shri Gusainji could not bear Kumbhandasji's anguish. Stepping outside, he told him: "Kumbhandas! Go back to the temple for Shri Govardhannathji's darshan—your journey abroad is already complete!" (Bhavprakash compares this to Gajjandhavan's viraha for Shri Navanitpriyaji and cites the Gita verse 'Ye yatha mam prapadyante tanstathaiva bhajamyaham', explaining that Shri Govardhannathji was equally pained in separation.)

Instantly consoled, Kumbhandasji bowed and ran back to the temple. As the doors opened for Utthapan darshan, he sang:

Raag Nat —
"Jopen chomp milan ki honi | to kyon rahyo pare suni sajani laakh kare kin koi ||1||
Jope virah paraspar vyaape to kachu jeeya bane | lok laaj kul ki maryada aiko chitta na gine ||2||
'Kumbhandas' jihin tan laagi aur kachu na suhaaya | Giridharlal toya binu dekhe chhin chhin kalpa vihaaya ||3||"

Pleased, Shri Govardhannathji told him: "Kumbhandas! Just as you cannot live without Me, I too cannot live without you; now you shall always stay near Me."

Varta — Prasang 7
Once Shri Gusainji playfully asked Kumbhandasji, "How many sons do you have?" Kumbhandasji answered, "Maharaj, I have one and a half sons!" Surprised, Shri Gusainji asked why, since he had heard of seven. Kumbhandasji explained: "Maharaj, five are attached to worldly life—what use are they? One full son is Chaturbhujdas, and half a son is Krishnadas, who serves Shri Govardhannathji's cows."

Bhavprakash — Though cow-seva is supreme, in Pushtimarg a complete Vaishnava experiences both sanyog rasa (direct service) and viprayog rasa (the bliss of separation). Krishnadas had cow-seva and darshan but not yet the experience of rahasya-lila, hence "half"; Chaturbhujdas experienced both sanyog and viprayog and sang lila kirtans, hence "one full son."

Shri Gusainji smiled warmly: "Kumbhandas, you spoke the truth—only a Bhagavadiya is truly a son."

Varta — Prasang 8
Kumbhandasji's son Krishnadas served as a cowherd for Shri Govardhannathji's cows. Returning one evening near Puchhari, a tiger emerged from a cave in Shri Girirajji. All the cows fled safely to the cowshed (khirak), except one large, heavy-uddered cow walking slowly behind. As the tiger charged it, Krishnadas shouted: "O wicked one! This is Shri Govardhannathji's cow; if you are hungry, come at me!" Driving the cow safely into the khirak, Krishnadas stood before the tiger and gave up his life.

At that very moment in the khirak, Gopinathdas Gwal and Kumbhandasji beheld a wondrous vision: Shri Govardhannathji Himself was milking that large cow while Krishnadas held its calf! Walking afterward toward the temple near Dandoti Shila, Kumbhandasji heard that the tiger had killed Krishnadas, and he collapsed in a dead faint.

People reported to Shri Gusainji that Krishnadas had died saving the cow and Kumbhandasji had fainted from grief over his son. Shri Gusainji first corrected them: "Do not say that! Shri Govardhannathji's cow will never abandon Krishnadas!" Finishing Anosar, Shri Gusainji came down to Dandoti Shila. When bystanders remarked that no one escapes the agony of losing a son, Shri Gusainji said: "He is not grieving for his son! He is grieving because ritual impurity (sutak) will keep him from Shri Govardhannathji's darshan!"

Calling out to him, Shri Gusainji declared: "Kumbhandas! Come tomorrow morning—I will give you Shri Govardhannathji's darshan!" Instantly Kumbhandasji rose, offered Dandavat, and said, "Maharaj! Who besides You knows my heart?" Shri Gusainji sent him to perform Krishnadas's last rites. In the Baithak, Gopinathdas Gwal confirmed the divine vision in the khirak. Next morning, Shri Gusainji gave Kumbhandasji the very first darshan—establishing from that day the Pushtimarg custom of allowing darshan even during sutak. After Bhog darshan, Kumbhandasji spent the sutak days in Parasoli singing viraha pads:

Raag Bihagaro —
"Tihare milan binu dukhit Gopal |
Ati aatur kulavadhu Braj-sundari pyaare-virah behaal ||1||
Seetal chand tapant dahat kiranani kamalapatra jal-janu vyaal |
Chandan kusum suhaaya na baadhi hai tan jvaal |
'Kumbhandas' nav tan Syam tum binu kanakalata sooki maanon greeshma kaal ||2||"

Raag Bihagaro —
"Ab dinaraat pahaarase bhae | tab ten nighatat naahin jab te Hari Madhupuri gae ||1||
Yah jaaniyat bidhata jug sam keene jaam nae | jaagat jaat bihaat na kyon hoo aise meet thae ||2||
Brajabaasi sab param deen ati vyaakul soch lae | jyon binu praan dukhit jalaruh gan daarun hride hae ||3||
'Kumbhandas' bichhuri Nandanandan bahu santaap dae | ab Giridhar binu rahat nirantar lochan neer chhae ||4||"

Raag Kedaro —
"Auranakon sameep bichhurano aayo mere hi hisa |
Sab koou sove apune sukh aali mokon chaahat jaaya chahun disa ||1||
Na jaanon ya bidhata ki gati mere aank likhe aise kaun risa |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu Giridhar kahate nisadin hi rate jyon chaatak ghan trisa ||2||"

Varta — Prasang 9
Once Shri Gokulnathji and Shri Balkrishnaji told Shri Gusainji that Kumbhandasji had never visited Shri Gokul and they wished to take him for Shri Navanitpriyaji's darshan. Shri Gusainji replied, "Try if you wish, but Kumbhandasji will never cross Shri Yamunaji."

On the bright night of Vaishakh Shukla 11, while Shri Gusainji was in Gokul, the two brothers took Kumbhandasji by the hand after Shayan Aarti and walked toward Shri Gokul, engaging him in deep Bhagavad-varta so he would not notice the journey. On the way, Shri Gokulnathji asked whether Shri Govardhannathji ever adorns (performs shringar for) Shri Swaminiji.

Absorbed in love, Kumbhandasji narrated an exquisite autumn (Ashwin) night lila: after gathering forest flowers and seating themselves on the shringar-chautara near the Rasmandal, Vishakhaji began Shri Swaminiji's shringar, when Shri Govardhannathji insisted on doing it Himself. Because neither could bear being without the sight of the other's face, clever Vishakhaji held a mirror before Shri Swaminiji. While weaving fine pearls into Shri Swaminiji's dark tresses, Shri Thakorji gazed at her moon-like reflection in rapture and accidentally let go of the braid—scattering pearls across the jeweled platform to the sakhis' laughter! Vishakhaji then held the braid while Shri Nathji completed the pearl and floral adornment, applying kajal, bindi, tilak, and mahavar to her feet; afterward Shri Swaminiji adorned Shri Govardhandhar.

So engrossed were they that they reached the bank of Shri Yamunaji opposite Gokul at dawn, just as Shri Gusainji crossed over by boat. Seeing Shri Gusainji, Kumbhandasji awoke to his surroundings, realized it was morning, let go of Shri Gokulnathji's hand, and bolted back toward Giriraj crying: "Alas! Who will sing the awakening kirtan for Shri Govardhannathji? My Seva is lost!" Shri Gokulnathji and the others ran after him in vain. Shri Gusainji smiled: "I told you he would never cross Yamunaji—and Shri Govardhannathji will not wake until Kumbhandas sings!" Mounting his saddled horse, Shri Gusainji caught up to Kumbhandasji and guided him back to Shri Girirajji. Meanwhile at the temple, Ramdas Bhitariya and all the sevaks kept accidentally becoming ritually defiled (chhuya) four times in a row and had to bathe a fifth time—all orchestrated by Shri Govardhannathji for Kumbhandasji's sake! Once Kumbhandasji sang the awakening pad, Shri Govardhannathji awoke. The next day was Nrisimha Chaturdashi.

Varta — Prasang 10
Once Kumbhandasji sat in his field at Parasoli while Shri Govardhannathji played right in front of him. When Utthapan time came, Kumbhandasji rose to go to the temple on Shri Girirajji. Shri Nathji asked, "I am playing right here with you; why are you going there?" Kumbhandasji replied: "Maharaj! Here You play out of Your own grace, and if You run away I have no hold on You; but in the temple Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji has installed You, so You cannot leave there. Indeed, it is solely by the glory of temple darshan that You grace me here, so I must go!" Laughing, Shri Govardhannathji said, "Kumbhandas, your devotion is extraordinary; I never leave you for an instant." Walking together as far as Govindkund until the conch blew, Shri Nathji entered the temple while Kumbhandasji climbed up via Anyor for darshan.

Varta — Prasang 11
One day a gardener brought a basket of two hundred gorgeous mangoes to Parasoli Chandrasarovar and wiped them clean. Arriving for water after Rajbhog Aarti, Kumbhandasji asked where he was taking them. The gardener said he would sell them in Mathura for ten rupees. Having no money, Kumbhandasji mentally offered all two hundred mangoes in mansi seva to Shri Govardhannathji, who invisibly accepted them.

In Mathura, a Rajput from Mat village bought all two hundred mangoes for ten rupees, gave half to his companion Sanadhya Brahmin, and each ate fifty by the Yamuna. That night both dreamed of Shri Govardhannathji. The Rajput—who in eternal Lila was 'Nena' Gopa, armed guardian of Nandarayji's cows, born on earth for killing a snake—was captivated. Giving his remaining mangoes, weapons, clothes, and five rupees to the Brahmin to guide him to Shri Girirajji, he had Shayan Aarti darshan, stood at Dandoti Shila wearing a single dhoti, and surrendered to Shri Gusainji.

Shri Gusainji told him: "Kumbhandasji's grace has fallen upon you through those mansi Mahaprasadi mangoes!" Granting him Naam and Brahmasambandh, Shri Gusainji gave him weapons, clothes, and a horse to guard Shri Nathji's cows. Soon Shri Nathji began giving him direct darshan among the cows, and he became a great Bhagavadiya, sending his two sons back to manage the household. (Bhavprakash also notes that Kumbhandasji's widowed niece was Vishakhaji's sakhi 'Sarovari' in Lila, who likewise enjoyed direct darshan of Shri Govardhannathji.)

Varta — Prasang 12
On Paush Krishna 8, Shri Govardhannathji thought: "Shri Gusainji celebrates My birthday with great splendor; tomorrow is Shri Gusainji's birthday, so I shall celebrate it too!" He instructed Ramdasji and Kumbhandasji to prepare jalebis. Sadu Pande supplied ghee and flour; having nothing at home, Kumbhandasji sold two male and two female buffalo calves for five rupees and gave the money to Ramdasji, while other sevaks added one or two rupees each (totaling 21 rupees for sugar). They fried jalebis all night. At dawn, after Abhyang, Shri Nathji wore saffron pag, vaga, and kulah sent by Shri Gusainji, and at the Lord's command Kumbhandasji sang Badhai pads:

Raag Devgandhar —
"Aaj badhaai Shri Vallabhdvaar |
Pragat bhae pooran Purushottam pushti karan vistaar ||1||
Bhaagi udai sab daivi jeevanake nihsaadhan jan kiye uddhaar |
'Kumbhandas' Giridharan jugal vapu nigam agam sab saadhan saar ||2||"

Raag Sarang —
"Pragat bhae Shri Vallabh aaya |
Seva ras vistaar karanakon goodh gyaan sab pragat dikhaaya ||1||
Nijajan sakal kiye paavan ghar bandanabaar bandhaaya |
'Kumbhandas' Giridhar gun mahima bandeejan chaaran gun gaaya ||2||"

Arriving from Gokul, Shri Gusainji saw baskets of jalebis and learned that Shri Govardhannathji had celebrated his birthday and that Kumbhandasji had contributed five rupees. Asking where Kumbhandasji got the money, Kumbhandasji replied with deep humility: "Maharaj! Where is my home? My home is at Your lotus feet! Two male and two female calves were extra, so I sold them. Only when one sells body, life, home, wife, and sons for Your sake is Vaishnava dharma fulfilled." Overcome with emotion, Shri Gusainji deeply praised Kumbhandasji's humility (dainyata).

Varta — Prasang 13
Once Kumbhandasji asked Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji about the principles of Pushtimarg. Shri Acharyaji graciously taught him the eighty-four offenses (Chaurasi Aparadh), the traits of rajasi, tamasi, and satviki devotees, the full daily Seva from morning to Shayan, and the essence of Bal-lila and Kishor-lila—remarking that only blessed Bhagavadiyas like him would inquire and practice it, as difficult times lay ahead when none would ask or speak of it. (Bhavprakash: Just as lioness's milk stays only in a golden vessel, the essence of Bhagavad-lila abides only in a Bhagavadiya's heart.)

Varta — Prasang 14
One day Kumbhandasji asked Shri Gusainji: "Maharaj! In my home are my wife, five of my seven sons, and seven daughters-in-law, yet none has firm bhagavadbhava—only my niece does. Why is this?"

Shri Gusainji narrated a Puranic tale to all the Vaishnavas: A Brahmin sent four different Brahmins to find a groom for his only daughter, and all four fixed separate matches for the exact same morning a month later, threatening to end their lives if he broke the betrothal. Weeping in despair by a river, the Brahmin met a compassionate Bhagavadiya who told him to catch the first animals that appeared the evening before the wedding and lock them in a room with his sleeping daughter. He caught a cat, a bitch, and a she-ass and locked them in with her. At the wedding hour, four identical brides stepped out and married the four grooms.

Later, to identify his real daughter, the Brahmin invited his four sons-in-law and asked about their wives' traits. The first said she barked like a dog; the second said she stole Shri Thakorji's food like a cat; the third said she stayed filthy and kicked like a donkey; the fourth praised her as Lakshmi herself—sweet-spoken and devoted to husband, Guru, Thakorji, and Vaishnavas. Thus the Brahmin recognized his true daughter.

Shri Gusainji concluded: "Kumbhandasji! Only one possessing Vaishnava qualities is truly human. What does mere human form matter? Ravana and Kumbhakarna became demons by their wicked deeds. One's true nature is known by one's conduct. Your niece is a great Bhagavadiya and will attain fulfillment through your satsang."

Varta — Prasang 15
In his final days, when his body grew very frail, Kumbhandasji sat at Sankarshankund near Anyor. Chaturbhujdasji offered to carry him in his lap to Jamunavata, but Kumbhandasji said his body would depart within a few ghadis and he would stay there.

Hearing this after Rajbhog Aarti, Shri Gusainji came to Sankarshankund and asked: "Kumbhandas! In which Lila is your mind absorbed right now?" Unable to rise, Kumbhandasji bowed his head in mental Dandavat and sang two pads:

Raag Sarang —
"Bisari gayo Lal karat go-dohan |
Nirakhi anoop chand mukh ikatak rahyo hai saanvaro Mohan ||1||
Nav naagari vichitra chatur gun ang ang roop suthohan |
'Kumbhandas' Lal Giridhar man haryo kateeli bhonhan ||2||"

Raag Sarang —
"Lal teri chitavani chit hi churaavati |
Nandagaam Vrishabhaanapura beech maarag chalan na paavati ||1||
Hon bhari hon dari ho nahin kaahoo Lalita drigan chalaavati |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu Govardhandhar dharyo so kyon na bataavat ||2||"

Shri Gusainji then asked: "Kumbhandas, you sang of this lila, now tell me where your innermost heart (antahkaran) truly abides." Then Kumbhandasji sang two Nikunj-lila pads before Shri Gusainji:

Raag Bihagaro —
"Toya milanakon bohot karat hai Mohanlal Govardhandhaari |
Uttar mohi deoo kin bhaamini kaha kahon hon baat tihaari ||1||
Dekhi too jo jharokhan ke mag tan sohat jhoomak saari |
Tan man baseeri Lal Giridhar ke ek chit ten tarat na taari |
Kahiri sakhi hon kihin mag aaoon too bataai de thaur suchaari |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu baithe tahaan dekhiyat hain jahaan oonchi chitrasaari ||2||"

Raag Bihagaro —
"Rasikanee rasamen rahati gadhi |
Kanak beli Vrishabhaan nandini Syam tamaal chadhi ||1||
Viharat Shri Giridharlal sang kaun paath padhi |
'Kumbhandas' Prabhu Shri Govardhandhar rati ras keli badhi ||2||"
(Immersed in the nectar of rasikas, the golden vine—Vrishabhanu's daughter—twines around the dark tamal tree. What lore has she mastered while sporting with Shri Giridharlal? Kumbhandas's Lord Shri Govardhandhar deepens the blissful play of love!)

Singing this pad, Kumbhandasji departed his mortal body and entered eternal Nikunj-lila at his gate near Anyor. Shri Gusainji returned to Gopalpur while Chaturbhujdasji and his brothers performed the last rites. Throughout the day from Utthapan to Shayan, Shri Gusainji remained silent and sorrowful. When Ramdasji asked why, Shri Gusainji said: "Such a supreme Bhagavadiya has departed; now the era of true devotees on earth has come to a close!"

Thus was Kumbhandasji a supremely blessed Bhagavadiya of Shri Acharyaji Mahaprabhuji, upon whom Shri Govardhannathji and Shri Gusainji were forever pleased. His Varta is boundless and beyond words—how far can it be told?
